body:
survivingTombstones admits only the local operator's tombstones (src/gateway/erase.ts ~193),
while a channel-lens as-of read resolves over the POOL's ground (src/gateway/reads.ts ~130,
216-224). If a pool ever loses a byte to a peer-authored erasure that ships no local operator
tombstone, the as-of window spans a forgetting the §26 annotation cannot see — the banner
promises "the past never pretends to a completeness it lost" and cannot keep it for federated
ground. annotateImpl is shared machinery, so the data doors and the rendered route (T208)
have the identical blind spot. Found by T208's erasure lens (2026-08-21); pre-existing.

This is half analysis, half build: today a peer cannot ORDER an erasure here (the door
refuses foreign removal-orders — §11), so the reachable shape is a pool RE-SEEDED from a peer
that erased upstream: bytes this store once held vanish from the pool on re-attach with no
tombstone anywhere. First establish the reachable states (re-attach semantics, T214's seam);
then either mint a local witness at the seam (a receiver-signed absence record when a
re-seed drops ids the pool previously held — custody's sibling) or widen the confession's
sources. The witness is the recommended direction: it keeps §11's authority boundary (no
foreign tombstone ever binds) while making the annotation honest.

Acceptance criteria (analysis first):
(a) The reachable no-tombstone-loss states are enumerated in the ticket/spec update, each
    with a fixture sketch. Verify: review at PR.
(b) For each reachable state, the §26 annotation names the window's incompleteness. Verify:
    tests named once (a) settles the mechanism.

Merge tier: the report-honesty side of erasure — self-merge for the witness/annotation;
anything touching what re-seeding DROPS is T214's design ground and waits with it.
title: The as-of confession is blind to a peer-authored forgetting in a channel pool
